author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ducati rider Marc Marquez won the San Marino Grand Prix sprint Saturday, beating Aprilia’s Marco Bezzecchi and cutting Jorge Martin’s MotoGP championship lead to 14 points. Martin finished third, keeping the title fight compressed ahead of Sunday’s full-distance race.

Bezzecchi started from pole after setting a lap record, but Marquez moved ahead at the first turn and controlled the 13-lap sprint. He reinforced the performance with a race-lap record on the penultimate tour. Bezzecchi’s runner-up finish leaves him 22 points behind Martin in third place in the standings, preserving a three-rider contest near the top.

Sprint points have made Saturdays increasingly important in MotoGP, and Marquez converted track position into a material championship gain without waiting for the main event. The result also demonstrated Ducati’s race pace against Aprilia’s qualifying speed. Sunday will offer more points and a longer strategic test, with tire management and launch execution likely to matter. For now, Marquez’s victory ensures the San Marino weekend will tighten rather than settle the title picture.
dek: The Ducati rider beat Marco Bezzecchi over 13 laps and moved within 14 points of MotoGP leader Jorge Martin.
headline: Marc Marquez wins San Marino sprint to tighten title race
